note: Hand-written, first draft 2026-11-17, for the Russian pilot. A broad transcription that shows what a learner cannot read off the spelling: vowel reduction, palatalization, devoicing.
conventions: Standard Russian as spoken in Moscow. Palatalization is written with ʲ after the consonant (нет is /ˈnʲet/). Unstressed vowels are written reduced: о and а are ɐ in the syllable before the stress and at the start of a word and ə elsewhere (молоко is /mə.lɐ.ˈko/), and two of them side by side before the stress are both ɐ (соответственно begins /sɐ.ɐt/); е and я after a soft consonant are ɪ (река is /rʲɪ.ˈka/). Unstressed и is always i and unstressed у always u, never ɪ or ʊ (мальчик is /ˈmalʲ.tɕik/, чемпионат is /tɕɪm.pʲi.ɐ.ˈnat/, искать is /i.ˈskatʲ/). ы is ɨ. A voiced consonant is written voiceless at the end of a word and before a voiceless one (хлеб is /ˈxlʲep/, водка is /ˈvot.kə/). ш and ж are ʂ and ʐ, щ is ɕː, ч is tɕ, ц is ts, hard л is l. A double letter is written long, with ː, only where it is said long (ванна is /ˈva.nːə/), and single where it is not. A letter that is not said is not written, and a letter said as another is written as it is said (солнце is /ˈson.tsə/, что is /ˈʂto/, его is /jɪ.ˈvo/).
